title: Multiple-testing thresholds

blocks.what_we_do: Compare the conventional GWAS threshold, scan-specific Bonferroni and false-discovery-rate adjustment.
blocks.why: Testing many null hypotheses creates many opportunities for false positives. Bonferroni divides a chosen family-wise error rate alpha by the number of tests; it controls the probability of at least one false rejection under its assumptions even when tests are dependent. The conventional 5e-8 threshold approximates 0.05 divided by one million common-variant tests; it is a convention, not a guarantee for every ancestry, sequencing design or analysis family. Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) targets a different quantity: the expected fraction of false discoveries among rejected tests under its conditions. Define the test family before inspecting results.
blocks.you_need: Valid additive results from 6.4; no replacement of failed p-values.
blocks.command:
```{r s7-4}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
p <- results$P[valid_p(results$P)]
threshold <- data.frame(rule = c("Conventional GWAS", "Bonferroni for this scan", "BH adjusted p at 0.05"),
  threshold = c(5e-8, 0.05 / length(p), 0.05),
  discoveries = c(sum(p < 5e-8), sum(p < 0.05 / length(p)), sum(p.adjust(p, method = "BH") < 0.05)))
print(threshold)
guided_write(threshold, guided_path(cfg, "7.4", "thresholds.tsv"))
```

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
236,815 finite tests imply a scan-specific Bonferroni threshold of approximately 2.11e-7. The conventional threshold gives eight discoveries. BH answers a different error-control question and may return more.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Does FDR 5% mean each reported variant has a 5% probability of being false?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. FDR is an expectation about the discovery set, not a posterior probability assigned to each variant.

</details>
